Mr. I. C. Herried August 10, 1973 Page 2
2. The Southeastern Wisconsin Regional Planning Commission has currently underway a regional airport system planning study to provide recommendations for the orderly development of public airport facilities within the Region. To date, that study has produced a series of airport system planning objectives, principles and standards; a forecast of aviation activity; and a series of alternative system plans to overcome known and projected facility deficiencies.
The forecasts of air carrier passengers originating within the Region require and support only one scheduled air carrier airport within the Region. General Mitchell Field, with its present capital facilities, location with respect to population concentrations and the Region's primary central business district, and other attributes consistent with the airport system planning objectives, principles, and standards, presents a most favorable alternative site for location of the Region's one air carrier airport.
The enplaning passenger growth forecast at General Mitchell Field, as developed under the Commission's airport system plan, ranges from a low of 3,182,000 to a high of 4,547,000 passengers per year in 1990. This compares to a forecast of 5,000,000 enplaning passengers per year developed by the Air Transport Association of America and the 5,400,000 enplaning passengers per year listed in the environmental statement. The forecast prepared under the Commission's system plan recognizes continued diversion to the Chicago airports of 20 to 25 percent of the commercial air passenger traffic generated within the Region, an expression of the competitiveness of airports in the personal and economic decisions of citizens and private enterprise.
The volume of air cargo handled through General Mitchell Field is expected to increase from 15,435 tons served in 1969 to 200,000 tons by 1990. The volume of mail is expected to increase from 6,409 tons in 1969 to 20,000 tons in 1990.
To serve these forecasted demands and recognizing the importance of integrating ground and air transportation, the Technical Coordinating and Advisory Committee for Airport System Planning adopted a series of objectives, principles, and standards which among other things, require that the main airport entrance road serving Primary Schedule Air Transport Airports such as General Mitchell Field be directly connected to a freeway on the state trunk highway system. The objectives further require that a scheduled air transport airport terminal shall be directly connected to the principle or central business district of the airport service area by intra-urban, rapid, or modified rapid transit facilities providing public passenger service
